entities.name: Liraglutide
observations: Improved islet graft performance in rodent transplantation models while reducing inflammatory chemokine/cytokine signaling and macrophage responses; causal mediation remains unproven.

entities.name: Islet graft function
observations: Liraglutide improved viability, glycemic control, glucose tolerance, and graft morphology in small-animal transplantation studies.

entities.name: Anti-inflammatory effects
observations: In rat islet transplantation, liraglutide reduced CCL2 and IL-6 secretion, macrophage chemotaxis/activation, and macrophage infiltration; IL-10 was unchanged.
GLP-1 agonist studies in isolated human and rodent islets showed reduced inflammatory cytokine-associated injury, but did not prove that inflammation reduction caused in-vivo graft benefit.

entities.name: PMID:27515367
observations: Rat islet transplantation study: improved graft viability/function and glycemia coincided with reduced CCL2/IL-6 signaling and macrophage recruitment; antioxidant effects were also observed. No selective inflammation-blocking or GLP-1R loss-of-function test established mediation.

entities.name: PMID:18511515
observations: Marginal-mass syngeneic mouse transplantation study: liraglutide accelerated normoglycemia, improved glucose tolerance, and reduced early graft beta-cell apoptosis; inflammatory markers were not reported in the available evidence.

entities.name: PMID:21669040
observations: Human-islet exenatide study: improved islet function and reduced inflammatory mediators and caspase-3 activation; partial exendin-9 blockade supported GLP-1R involvement, but causal mediation of graft benefit was not established.

entities.name: PMID:26794660
observations: Rodent and human islet cytokine-challenge study: exendin-4 protected against cytokine-induced apoptosis and dysfunction; in-vitro design did not establish mediation of liraglutide's in-vivo graft effects.

entities.name: PMID:40956865
observations: Syngeneic mouse study using a liraglutide-releasing silk-fibroin scaffold: improved normoglycemia, graft morphology, and viability with protection from inflammatory injury; biomaterial effects confounded attribution to anti-inflammatory action.
